title: Two Sum
description: Given an array of integers and a target, return the indices of the two numbers that add up to the target. Exactly one solution exists.
hints: Have you tried a hash map of value → index?
notes: Check the map BEFORE inserting, otherwise you can pair an element with itself.
approach: Scan the array once, and for every value check whether (target - value) was already seen; store each value's index in a hash map as you go.

title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
description: You get one buy and one sell on a daily price list. Return the maximum profit, or 0 if no profit is possible.
notes: The min-so-far IS the optimal buy for every later day.
approach: Track the minimum price seen so far while sweeping left to right; at each day compute profit against that minimum and keep the best.

title: Maximum Subarray
description: Find the contiguous segment with the largest sum and return that sum. The array may contain negatives.

examples.explanation: The subarray [4,-1,2,1] has the largest sum 6.

hints: Kadane's algorithm: best ending here vs restart here.
notes: If all numbers are negative the answer is the largest single element — restart rule handles it.
approach: Kadane: keep the best sum ending here; if it drops below the current element, restart the segment there.

notes: Two-pointer swap version avoids the second pass.
approach: Maintain a write pointer that only advances when we copy a non-zero value; fill the tail with zeroes afterwards.

notes: Two passes — prefix pass writes the answer, suffix pass multiplies in.
approach: Prefix products from the left, then multiply by suffix products sweeping back from the right.

title: Rotate Array
description: Rotate the array to the right by k steps, in place.
notes: k %= n first, otherwise huge k overflows the logic.
approach: Reverse the whole array, then reverse the first k and the rest — the classic three-reversal trick.

title: Merge Sorted Array
description: Merge a second sorted array into the first one which has enough trailing space, keeping the result sorted.
notes: Backwards fill is what makes it in-place.
approach: Fill from the back comparing the largest remaining elements so no value is ever overwritten.

title: Trapping Rain Water
description: Given bar heights, compute how many units of water are held between the bars after rain.
notes: leftMax/rightMax are what you must never forget; the stack variant does the same per-column.
approach: Two pointers: water at a column is bounded by the smaller side's max — move the side with the smaller maximum inward.

title: Valid Anagram
description: Decide whether two strings are anagrams of each other (same characters, same frequencies, any order).
notes: Length check first — cheap early exit.
approach: Count character frequencies of the first string, decrement with the second, and check everything is zero.

title: Longest Common Prefix
description: Find the longest string prefix shared by every string in a list.
notes: Column-wise scanning works too, but template shrinking is shorter to code.
approach: Use the first string as a template and shorten it until it is a prefix of every other string.

title: Longest Palindromic Substring
description: Return the longest contiguous substring that reads the same forwards and backwards.
notes: Manacher is O(n) but expand-around-centre is what interviews expect unless asked otherwise.
approach: Expand around every index as a centre (odd and even widths) and keep the widest successful expansion.

title: String Compression
description: Compress a character array into run-length form (a2b1c3) in place, returning the new length.
notes: Counts >= 10 must be written digit by digit — easy to forget.
approach: Two pointers: a read pointer walks runs, a write pointer emits char + count digits only when the run exceeds 1.

title: Group Anagrams
description: Group a list of strings so each group contains only anagrams of one another.
notes: Sorting each word gives O(k log k) per word; counting signature is O(k).
approach: Use the sorted string (or a 26-count signature) as the hash key and bucket words by it.

title: Top K Frequent Elements

title: Longest Consecutive Sequence

notes: Only start from run beginnings — that is what keeps it O(n).
approach: Put everything in a set; only start counting at numbers whose predecessor is absent, then walk forward.

notes: Define what lo/hi mean BEFORE writing the loop — always maintain the search invariant.
approach: Maintain [lo, hi] inclusive; mid = lo + floor((hi - lo) / 2) and shrink whichever side cannot contain the target.

title: Find Peak Element

notes: You are searching a predicate, not a value — that is allowed even without sorting.
